response.title: Define attestation schemas and shared fixtures
response.objective: Freeze the protocol contracts and cross-language fixtures that every later component depends on.
scope: Create versioned JSON schemas for policy, attestors registry, predicate, and IPC.
Implement strict policy and registry parsers in Swift and Python with duplicate-key and resource-limit enforcement.
Add golden fixtures for DSSE statements, PAE bytes, keys, signatures, snapshot digests, and configuration errors.
implementation_steps: Add JSON schemas under attestation/schemas/ for policy-v1, attestors-v1, predicate-v1, and ipc-v1, encoding the field shapes and constraints from sections 4, 7, and 8.

Implement strict YAML parsers in Swift (using Yams with event auditing) and Python (using PyYAML with a custom loader) that reject duplicate keys, aliases, anchors, custom tags, unknown fields, and enforce size/step limits.
Implement raw-blob SHA-256 hashing, key fingerprint computation, snapshot record encoding, and step-definition digest computation in both languages, with unit tests.

Add fixture generators and golden files under attestation/fixtures/ covering valid and invalid policies, registries, snapshot digests, DSSE PAE bytes, and signed statements; wire them into attestation/scripts/verify-all.sh.
acceptance_criteria: 01-AC1: The sample Make and shell policies parse identically in Swift and Python; exact byte digests and ordered IDs match the frozen fixtures.
01-AC2: Every forbidden schema condition in section 4 has a rejecting fixture exercised by both implementations, including duplicate YAML keys and aliases.
01-AC3: Two fixtures with different YAML formatting have different raw policy digests even when their parsed meaning matches.
01-AC4: Snapshot digest fixtures cover ordinary files, executable files, symlinks, empty files, non-ASCII paths, and differing sort orders.
01-AC5: Unknown protocol/schema versions, floats in integer fields, oversized inputs, malformed dates, and key/fingerprint mismatches fail explicitly.
